mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which is typically associated with economic expansion and positive equity returns. This mechanism assumes that labor market strength translates to consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving S&P 500 returns higher over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns during periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4%) in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending. This leads to downward pressure on equity valuations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases when FEDFUNDS > 5%, or the mechanism's Rank IC is not significantly positive during monetary tightening periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in the last 3 months and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases, it signals a tightening labor market with higher borrowing costs. This combination creates headwinds for equity markets, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5pp in 3 months AND UNRATE decreases
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of triggered cases, or the mechanism's Rank IC is not significantly negative during late-cycle expansions.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) relative to its 12-month moving average indicates strong consumer demand, which is typically associated with economic expansion and positive equity returns. This mechanism assumes that strong demand translates to higher corporate revenues and earnings, driving S&P 500 returns higher over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns during periods of high RSAFS (above its 12-month moving average) in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a strong supply chain and manufacturing sector, which is typically associated with economic expansion and positive equity returns. This mechanism assumes that strong industrial activity translates to higher corporate revenues and earnings, driving S&P 500 returns higher over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns during periods of industrial production growth (INDPRO > 5-year average) in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic growth, which is typically associated with inflationary pressures. This mechanism assumes that high GDP growth leads to tighter monetary policy, increasing borrowing costs and reducing consumer and business spending, which drives S&P 500 returns lower over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of triggered cases, or the mechanism's Rank IC is not significantly negative during periods of high GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: When non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 100,000 jobs in a month and housing starts (HOUST) also increase, it signals a strong labor market and expanding economy. This combination is typically associated with higher consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving S&P 500 returns higher over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of triggered cases, or the mechanism's Rank IC is not significantly positive during economic expansions.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below its 5-year average and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is stable, it indicates an accommodative monetary policy that supports equity valuations. This mechanism assumes that low interest rates and controlled inflation lead to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of triggered cases, or the mechanism's Rank IC is not significantly positive during monetary easing periods.
